chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Badr, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever recites 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' once, blessings are bestowed upon him; and whoever recites it twice, blessings are bestowed upon him and his family; and whoever recites it three times, blessings are bestowed upon him, his family, and his neighbors.
And whoever recites it twelve times, Allah builds for him twelve castles in Paradise, so the Preservers (angels) say: 'Go with us to the castle of our brother so-and-so, so that we may look at it.'
And whoever recites it one hundred times, his sins of twenty-five years are forgiven him, apart from blood (shedding) and wealth (misappropriation).
And whoever recites it four hundred times, he has the reward of four hundred martyrs, each of whom had his horse hamstrung and his blood shed.
And whoever recites it a thousand times in a day and night, he will not die until he sees his seat in Paradise, or it is shown to him.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say, He is Allah, the One (Opening of Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas multiple times according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the spiritual potency of Surah Al-Ikhlas through a graduated scale of rewards, reflecting the Shia tradition of linking specific dhikr counts to tangible metaphysical benefits. The progression from personal blessing to the construction of twelve castles in Paradise illustrates the concept of *barakah* extending to one's household and neighbors, while the promise of forgiveness for twenty-five years highlights the surah's role in expiating minor sins. This narration underscores the practical devotional life in Shia Islam, where consistent recitation serves as both a means of spiritual purification and a guarantee of high status in the Hereafter.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Badr, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

The one who recites [112:1] Say He Allah is One (Chapter 112) once, would have Blessings upon him; and the one who recites it twice would have Blessings upon him and upon his family. And the one who recites it three times would have Blessings upon him, and upon his family, and upon his neighbours.

And the one who recites it twelve times, Allah would Build for him twelve castles in the Paradise. So the preservers (Angels) would be saying: ‘Come with us to the castle of our brother so and so, to look at it’.
And the one who recites it one hundred times, his sins of twenty five years would be Forgiven for him, apart from the (shedding of unlawful) blood, and the wealth.
And the one who recites it four hundred times, would have for him the Recompense of four hundred martyrs having had hamstrung their horses (not to let it fall into enemy hands) and shed its blood.
And the one who recites it a thousand times in a day and night, would not die until he sees his seat in the Paradise, or it is shown to him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Badr from Muhammad ibn Marwan from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Whoever reads Chapter 1 12 of the Holy Quran once receives blessings. Whoever reads it twice, he and his family receive blessings. Whoever reads it three times, he, his family and his neighbors receive blessings.
Whoever reads it twelve times, Allah will build for him twelve palaces in paradise and the keepers will say, ‘We should go and see the palaces of our brother so and so.’
Whoever reads it one hundred times his sins of twenty-five years will be forgiven, except murders and properties.
Whoever reads it four hundred times will receive a reward equal to that for four hundred martyrs, each of whom martyred after the destruction of his horse.
Whoever reads it one thousand times in one day and night will not die before seeing his place in paradise or is shown for him (to a third party).”’
